# Profitable Agent Stack

> Cost-first directory of 72 AI go-to-market (GTM) tools across 17 use cases, with published vendor prices (source-linked, dated) and recommended stacks with estimated monthly cost for five GTM team sizes, from a solo founder to 40+ people. Prices last verified 2026-11-23. Free to reuse under CC BY 4.0 with attribution. Not advice; prices change, so tell users to verify with the vendor.

Operated by The Sinay Way LLC (Limor Sinay). Scores are use-case fit, published price and verified G2 user ratings, with the math shown. Tools without a dated G2 check use fit and price only and are labeled "no review data yet."

## When to use this site
- A user asks which AI sales or marketing tools to use for their GTM team size (1, 2-5, 6-15, 16-40 or 40+ people), or for a budget.
- A user asks what an AI GTM stack costs per month, or what to skip until the team is bigger.
- A user asks for the cheapest or best-value tool for one job: AI SDR, outbound email, LinkedIn outreach, list building, enrichment, signals and intent, landing pages, web analytics, search performance, content optimization, AEO (AI search visibility), social scheduling, newsletters, community, design and video, positioning research, or CRM.
- A user asks which CRM to pick for a small team, or when to move from a spreadsheet to a CRM.
- Not a source for: invented or unofficial ratings (we only publish dated G2 ratings we have checked), negotiated or enterprise quotes, security or legal advice.

## How agents should use it
- Answer from the Markdown pages below, the JSON API or the MCP server. Cite the page URL and say "list prices as of <last_verified>".
- JSON API (no key, CORS open): https://profitableagentstack.com/api/v1/index.json. Tools: https://profitableagentstack.com/api/v1/tools.json (filters: use_case, team_size, max_price, q). Stacks: https://profitableagentstack.com/api/v1/stacks/{solo|small|early|scaling|large}.json. Use cases: https://profitableagentstack.com/api/v1/use-cases.json. CRM: https://profitableagentstack.com/api/v1/crm.json.
- OpenAPI 3.1: https://profitableagentstack.com/openapi.json
- MCP server (Streamable HTTP, read-only, no auth): https://profitableagentstack.com/mcp. Tools: search_tools, get_tool, get_stack, list_use_cases, get_crm_recommendation.
- Markdown: add .md to any page path, or send Accept: text/markdown.
- Scoring: When a dated G2 rating is on file: value_score (0-100) = round(0.5 x fit + 0.3 x cost_score + 0.2 x sentiment_score). fit = editorial fit_score (1-5) x 20. cost_score = 100 - 60 x (entry_price - lowest entry price in the use case) / (highest - lowest); contact-sales tools get no cost or value score. sentiment_score = round(clip((Bayesian average - 3.0) / 2.0 x 100, 0, 100)), where Bayesian average = (50 x 4.3 + review_count x G2 rating) / (50 + review_count). Tools without review data are labeled "no review data yet" and keep value_score = round(0.625 x fit + 0.375 x cost_score). The category-wide value score uses the overall G2 rating. When segment ratings exist later, stack pages prefer the rating for that team size (solo/small -> small business, early/scaling -> mid-market, large -> enterprise). Stack picks also weigh fit for the GTM team size (reviewer company-size mix, case studies, enterprise-readiness evidence).
- Links marked link_is_affiliate are affiliate links; they never change scores or order.

## Answers and guides
- [Quick answers: best stack by team size, cheapest tool per use case, CRM picks](https://profitableagentstack.com/answers.md)
- [Directory of all tools](https://profitableagentstack.com/directory.md)
- [New releases and price changes](https://profitableagentstack.com/new-releases.md)
- [Smartlead vs Instantly vs lemlist: which outbound tool fits a small GTM team?](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/smartlead-vs-instantly-vs-lemlist.md): Smartlead, Instantly and lemlist are outbound email sequencers, not full autonomous AI SDRs. For a 2–5 person GTM team, Instantly starts at $47/mo on Growth (email-only, 5,000 emails); Smartlead’s Base plan starts at $39/mo and is built around many mailboxes; lemlist’s Email plan starts at $69/mo monthly ($55 annual) and adds LinkedIn and other channels on Multichannel ($109/mo, or $87 annual). Salesforge (from $48/mo) and Woodpecker are other published-price options in the same use case. List prices last verified 2026-11-23; always verify with the vendor. Not advice.
- [How real companies use AI for GTM (sourced results)](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/how-companies-use-ai-for-gtm.md): Named companies have published what happened after they put AI into go-to-market, and the pattern is consistent: AI scales a motion that already works, and it takes daily human training. SaaStr’s first-party posts say agents first-touch-sourced $4.8 million in added pipeline and $2.4 million in closed-won revenue after eight months, with 15–20 hours of management a week from each of two leaders. Vendor-published stories from monday.com, Payhawk, Pump.co and Asana report time savings and pipeline or booking gains, each cited to the original page below. This is not advice; verify with the sources, and treat vendor case studies as the vendor’s account.
- [When to add AEO (AI search visibility) vs classic SEO](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/when-to-add-aeo.md): AEO tools track whether ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google's AI answers mention your brand. Classic search tools come first; add AEO when AI assistants already send you visits.
- [Why we size stacks by GTM team size, not funding stage](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/stacks-by-gtm-team-size.md): Funding rounds say little about what tools you need. How many people do go-to-market says a lot.
- [When to skip intent data (and what to do first)](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/when-to-skip-intent-data.md): Intent and signals tools help you prioritize. If you have nobody worth prioritizing yet, they are an expensive distraction.
- [One tool per job: how to stop paying twice](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/one-tool-per-job.md): Most GTM stacks pay for the same job two or three times. Here is how we pick one tool per job and explain each pick.
- [How we score AI GTM tools (and why cost counts)](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/how-we-score.md): The value score in plain words: what goes in, what does not, and why money never changes rank.

# Full text (generated 2026-11-23)

## Scoring methodology
When a dated G2 rating is on file: value_score (0-100) = round(0.5 x fit + 0.3 x cost_score + 0.2 x sentiment_score). fit = editorial fit_score (1-5) x 20. cost_score = 100 - 60 x (entry_price - lowest entry price in the use case) / (highest - lowest); contact-sales tools get no cost or value score. sentiment_score = round(clip((Bayesian average - 3.0) / 2.0 x 100, 0, 100)), where Bayesian average = (50 x 4.3 + review_count x G2 rating) / (50 + review_count). Tools without review data are labeled "no review data yet" and keep value_score = round(0.625 x fit + 0.375 x cost_score). The category-wide value score uses the overall G2 rating. When segment ratings exist later, stack pages prefer the rating for that team size (solo/small -> small business, early/scaling -> mid-market, large -> enterprise). Stack picks also weigh fit for the GTM team size (reviewer company-size mix, case studies, enterprise-readiness evidence).

- Use case: List building & lead data (list-building)
- Fits GTM team sizes: Solo founder (1 GTM person), Small GTM team (2–5 GTM people), Early scaling (6–15 GTM people), Scaling (16–40 GTM people), Large / multi-team (40+ GTM people)
- Price: Free Starter plan (no time limit; Apollo's FAQ calls it for 'exploring or very light usage'); Basic $49, Professional $79, Organization $119 per seat/mo billed annually (Organization: 3-seat minimum, SSO listed in plan table); Custom plan for SSO, advanced security and custom volumes via sales (entry USD 0/mo)
- Last verified: 2026-11-16
- Pricing source: https://www.apollo.io/pricing
- Scores: fit 5/5 (editorial), cost 100, sentiment 85, value 97 (best value in its use case)
- Reviews: G2 4.7/5 from 9,864 reviews, checked 2026-11-23 (https://www.g2.com/products/apollo-io/reviews)
- In our recommended stacks: Solo founder, Small GTM team, Early scaling, Scaling, Large / multi-team
- Page: https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/list-building#apollo

1 GTM person

# Solo founder: AI GTM stack for 1 GTM person, about $41/mo

About $41/mo + €19 Waalaxy for our recommended stack, estimated from published list prices as of 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-23 (per tool). Assumptions: 1 GTM person, 1 LinkedIn account, light volume. Hunter's free plan (50 credits/mo) caps how many new emails you can find; move up when you outgrow it. Monthly billing, entry tiers; Carrd is priced yearly ÷ 12. Actual cost depends on your usage, billing period, taxes and add-ons.

## Who this is for

One person doing all of go-to-market: you are the founder, the seller and the marketer. Your goal is the first repeatable customers, not a machine.

## Recommended stack (estimate)

One tool per job, no paid overlap. Each pick weighs two things: its value score and whether it fits a team of this size, judged from reviews by companies of similar size and from enterprise-readiness evidence. The value score is a category-wide number based on each tool's lowest published price (often a free plan), so a tool can be "best in category" and still not be the pick at this size. "Best in category" means the highest value score (ties included) among all tools we list for that use case.

- **Warm network & referrals.** Spreadsheet or notes app you already own. Message everyone you know who fits your ICP first; no tool is needed to do this.
- **ICP & positioning.** Customer conversations plus a one-page doc. We list no paid tool for this job: talk to buyers first.

| Use case | Best-value pick | Tier / assumption | Est. $/mo | Why this pick |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Sales stack** | | | | |
| List building & lead data | **[Apollo](https://www.apollo.io/)** value 97 · best in category | Free Starter plan | $0 | Highest value score for list building (free, fit 5/5). Exa is a free alternative if you prefer search-style prospecting. Free-plan limits change, so check them. |
| Enrichment & verification | **[Hunter](https://hunter.io/)** value 84 | Free plan (50 credits) | $0 | Free email finding and verification is enough for light hand-built lists. |
| Outbound email / sequencing | **[Smartlead](https://profitableagentstack.com/go/smartlead) affiliate** value 84 | Base, 1 workspace | $39 | Lowest published entry price for outbound email in our list. Instantly scores higher on value (93 vs 84) but costs $8 more; revisit at 2–5 people. |
| LinkedIn outreach | **[Waalaxy](https://profitableagentstack.com/go/waalaxy) affiliate** value 85 · best in category | 1 user × €19 (EUR, not converted) | $0 | Cheapest listed LinkedIn tool and the best value score in its category. Per user, billed in euros. |
| **Marketing stack** | | | | |
| Landing pages & websites | **[Carrd](https://carrd.com/)** value 84 | Pro Standard, $19/yr ÷ 12 | $1.58 | Cheapest custom-domain landing page in our list; $19/yr is the yearly price on its Pro page. |
| Newsletters | **[beehiiv](https://profitableagentstack.com/go/beehiiv) affiliate** value 94 · best in category | Free plan | $0 | Highest value score; free until you monetize. Kit is the free alternative (free up to 10,000 subscribers). |
| Web analytics | **[Google Analytics](https://marketingplatform.google.com/about/analytics/)** value 85 · best in category | Free | $0 | Free and good enough for basic traffic and source tracking at this size. |

## CRM for this team size (separate from the stack)

For 1 GTM person: **[HubSpot Sales Hub](https://www.hubspot.com/products/crm)**, Google Sheet first, then HubSpot Free CRM (up to 2 users) when a signal below appears, about **$0**. Runner-up: **[Attio](https://attio.com/)**, Free plan (up to 3 users), about $0. Not included in the stack total above.

|  | CRM | Tier / assumption | Est. cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pick | **[HubSpot Sales Hub](https://www.hubspot.com/products/crm)** | Google Sheet first, then HubSpot Free CRM (up to 2 users) when a signal below appears | $0 |
| Runner-up | **[Attio](https://attio.com/)** | Free plan (up to 3 users) | $0 |

HubSpot Sales Hub has the largest small-business reviewer base among the CRMs we checked (60.5% of its G2 reviewers are small businesses) and native integrations with Apollo, Hunter, Smartlead and Waalaxy. Attio suits founders who want a flexible data model.

Also worth a look: Zoho CRM Free (3 users), Bigin by Zoho Free (1 user) and Close Solo ($9/mo billed annually, built-in calling) also fit here.

### Spreadsheet or CRM?

A sheet is usually enough while you are the only person selling, live deals stay under about 20 and most come from your network. Move to a free CRM the week you turn on a sequencer, or once a follow-up slips.

Signals that it is time for a CRM (our rules of thumb, not benchmarks):

- **A second person works the pipeline.** A cofounder, first seller, contractor SDR or agency. Shared sheets struggle with ownership, duplicates and overwritten notes.
- **More than about 20–30 live deals or conversations at once.** Or a follow-up has slipped more than once.
- **You copy sequencer replies into the sheet by hand.** More than about 30 minutes a week. Most CRMs here receive replies from Instantly, Smartlead or lemlist directly.
- **Email and LinkedIn reach the same people.** One record per person stops you double-touching prospects.
- **Investor or board pipeline reporting takes more than about an hour a month.** Stage history and pipeline reports are built into every CRM listed, including free plans (depth varies).
- **Inbound leads arrive or your first sales hire starts.** Forms, routing and activity history make the handoff work.

Starter sheet columns: Company, Contact, Email, LinkedIn URL, Source, Stage, Next step, Next-step date, Deal value, Last touch, Notes. Every CRM listed imports a CSV, so nothing is lost when you switch. List prices as of 2026-11-10 from vendor pricing pages; verify with the vendor. Seat counts follow this page's assumptions. [All CRMs we list](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/crm).

## Use cases that matter at this size

- List building & lead data
- Enrichment & verification
- Outbound email / sequencing
- LinkedIn outreach
- Landing pages & websites
- Newsletters
- Web analytics

## Skip for now

- **Signals & intent data (RB2B, PostHog, Common Room).** Paid intent and visitor-identification tools tell you who to talk to. Until hand-built outbound gets replies, you have nobody to prioritize.
- **AI SDR / agentic SDR.** These are contact-sales products. An agent cannot fix messaging that does not work by hand yet.
- **Social scheduling, search and content tools, design/video, community.** Useful later; none of them is needed to get the first customers. Free Search Console is worth setting up when you publish.
- **AEO (AI search visibility) tools.** No AI-search demand to measure yet, and warm leads and outbound come first. Revisit when content gets traffic.

# Small GTM team: AI GTM stack for 2–5 GTM people, about $106/mo

About $106/mo + €38 Waalaxy (2 users) for our recommended stack, estimated from published list prices as of 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-23 (per tool). Assumptions: 3 GTM people, 2 LinkedIn users, ~5,000 emails/mo, monthly billing, entry tiers. Waalaxy is priced per user in euros and not converted. Actual cost depends on your usage, billing period, taxes and add-ons.

## Who this is for

Two to five people share go-to-market. Warm intros and hand outbound already produce some meetings, and you now want a repeatable sequence plus a little content.

## Recommended stack (estimate)

One tool per job, no paid overlap. Each pick weighs two things: its value score and whether it fits a team of this size, judged from reviews by companies of similar size and from enterprise-readiness evidence. The value score is a category-wide number based on each tool's lowest published price (often a free plan), so a tool can be "best in category" and still not be the pick at this size. "Best in category" means the highest value score (ties included) among all tools we list for that use case.

- **Warm network & referrals.** Still your best channel. Keep it in a shared spreadsheet or your CRM.
- **ICP & positioning.** Revisit with real call notes; no paid tool listed for this job.

## CRM for this team size (separate from the stack)

For 2–5 GTM people: **[HubSpot Sales Hub](https://www.hubspot.com/products/crm)**, Free if 2 people work deals; Starter for 3 (3 seats × $20 list), about **$0–$60/mo**. Runner-up: **[Pipedrive](https://www.pipedrive.com/)**, Lite, 3 seats × $14 billed annually ($24 monthly), about $42–$72/mo. Not included in the stack total above.

|  | CRM | Tier / assumption | Est. cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pick | **[HubSpot Sales Hub](https://www.hubspot.com/products/crm)** | Free if 2 people work deals; Starter for 3 (3 seats × $20 list) | $0–$60/mo |
| Runner-up | **[Pipedrive](https://www.pipedrive.com/)** | Lite, 3 seats × $14 billed annually ($24 monthly) | $42–$72/mo |

HubSpot integrates natively with Instantly, Hunter, Apollo and Waalaxy, so replies and meetings can log themselves. HubSpot currently shows a limited-time lower Starter price for new customers; we use list price. Pipedrive is a strong choice for a simple visual pipeline (75.1% of its G2 reviewers are small businesses).

Also worth a look: Attio and Zoho CRM are free for up to 3 users. Close Essentials ($35/user/mo billed annually) fits phone-heavy teams.

### Spreadsheet or CRM?

A shared sheet can work for a short while, but at 2–5 a second person usually already works the pipeline, which is the clearest signal to add a CRM.

Signals that it is time for a CRM (our rules of thumb, not benchmarks):

- **A second person works the pipeline.** A cofounder, first seller, contractor SDR or agency. Shared sheets struggle with ownership, duplicates and overwritten notes.
- **More than about 20–30 live deals or conversations at once.** Or a follow-up has slipped more than once.
- **You copy sequencer replies into the sheet by hand.** More than about 30 minutes a week. Most CRMs here receive replies from Instantly, Smartlead or lemlist directly.
- **Email and LinkedIn reach the same people.** One record per person stops you double-touching prospects.
- **Investor or board pipeline reporting takes more than about an hour a month.** Stage history and pipeline reports are built into every CRM listed, including free plans (depth varies).
- **Inbound leads arrive or your first sales hire starts.** Forms, routing and activity history make the handoff work.

Starter sheet columns: Company, Contact, Email, LinkedIn URL, Source, Stage, Next step, Next-step date, Deal value, Last touch, Notes. Every CRM listed imports a CSV, so nothing is lost when you switch. List prices as of 2026-11-10 from vendor pricing pages; verify with the vendor. Seat counts follow this page's assumptions. [All CRMs we list](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/crm).

## Use cases that matter at this size

- List building & lead data
- Enrichment & verification
- Outbound email / sequencing
- LinkedIn outreach
- Search performance
- Social scheduling
- Landing pages & websites
- Newsletters
- Web analytics
- Signals, intent & analytics

## Skip for now

- **Paid signals & intent data.** Use at most the free RB2B plan, and only once outbound is booking meetings.
- **AI SDR / agentic SDR.** Contact-sales pricing and little to feed it yet.
- **Content optimization (Surfer), video, community.** Use Search Console and publish first; add paid content tools once content is a weekly habit.
- **AEO (AI search visibility) tools.** Skip until AI assistants send you visits you can see in analytics; warm leads and outbound still produce more pipeline than AI-search visibility.

About $913/mo for our recommended stack, estimated from published list prices as of 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-23 (per tool). Actual cost depends on your usage, billing period, taxes and add-ons.

## Who this is for

Six to fifteen people run go-to-market: dedicated sellers, someone owning content, and enough volume that tooling gaps cost real pipeline.

## Recommended stack (estimate)

One tool per job, no paid overlap. Each pick weighs two things: its value score and whether it fits a team of this size, judged from reviews by companies of similar size and from enterprise-readiness evidence. The value score is a category-wide number based on each tool's lowest published price (often a free plan), so a tool can be "best in category" and still not be the pick at this size. "Best in category" means the highest value score (ties included) among all tools we list for that use case.

- **Warm network & referrals.** Track in your CRM; keep investing, it is still your cheapest channel.
- **ICP & positioning.** Refresh quarterly from win/loss notes; no paid tool listed.

Also worth a look: Zoho CRM Standard ($14/user/mo billed annually) is a lower-cost option with native Hunter, lemlist and Smartlead integrations.

### Spreadsheet or CRM?

At 6–15 GTM people a shared sheet is rarely enough: several people work deals and replies arrive from more than one channel.

Signals that it is time for a CRM (our rules of thumb, not benchmarks):

- **A second person works the pipeline.** A cofounder, first seller, contractor SDR or agency. Shared sheets struggle with ownership, duplicates and overwritten notes.
- **More than about 20–30 live deals or conversations at once.** Or a follow-up has slipped more than once.
- **You copy sequencer replies into the sheet by hand.** More than about 30 minutes a week. Most CRMs here receive replies from Instantly, Smartlead or lemlist directly.
- **Email and LinkedIn reach the same people.** One record per person stops you double-touching prospects.
- **Investor or board pipeline reporting takes more than about an hour a month.** Stage history and pipeline reports are built into every CRM listed, including free plans (depth varies).
- **Inbound leads arrive or your first sales hire starts.** Forms, routing and activity history make the handoff work.

Starter sheet columns: Company, Contact, Email, LinkedIn URL, Source, Stage, Next step, Next-step date, Deal value, Last touch, Notes. Every CRM listed imports a CSV, so nothing is lost when you switch. List prices as of 2026-11-10 from vendor pricing pages; verify with the vendor. Seat counts follow this page's assumptions. [All CRMs we list](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/crm).

## Use cases that matter at this size

- List building & lead data
- Enrichment & verification
- Outbound email / sequencing
- LinkedIn outreach
- Signals, intent & analytics
- Search performance
- Content optimization
- AEO (AI search visibility)
- Social scheduling
- Landing pages & websites
- Newsletters
- Web analytics
- Product & funnel analytics

## Skip for now

- **AI SDR / agentic SDR.** Optional and contact-sales. Hire or train humans first; add an agent only when the motion is proven and measured.
- **Paid intent platforms (Common Room).** $2,500/mo billed annually is poor value until you have enough volume for multi-channel intent to change who you call.
- **Community, video.** Only if a specific channel is already working.
- **Content optimization at higher tiers; AEO beyond Peec Starter.** Start at the entry tiers; more prompts and models only when AI-search referrals show up in analytics.

## What we found: who reviews our list-building and enrichment picks (as of 2026-11-05)

Security and plan statements come from each vendor's own pages and are vendor claims; reviewer company-size shares come from G2's public comparison pages . Overall G2 star ratings and review counts, when we have a dated check, appear on each tool card and feed the sentiment part of the value score. Company-size segment ratings are not in the file yet (G2 product pages were blocked). Everything may change; confirm security, SSO and compliance in writing before buying. This is not legal or compliance advice.

- **Apollo (list building).** Pricing page (checked 2026-11-05): Basic $49, Professional $79 per seat/mo billed annually. G2: of 9,858 reviews, 28.4% mid-market (51-1,000 employees) and 4.6% enterprise, so most reviewers are smaller teams but the mid-market base is large. [Source](https://www.apollo.io/pricing)
- **Hunter vs Clay (enrichment).** G2 comparison (checked 2026-11-05): Hunter has 659 reviews (31.9% mid-market); Clay has 234 (24.8% mid-market, 1.4% enterprise). Clay's reviewers cite a learning curve and credit use. Neither review base is clearly mid-market-led, so we keep the cheaper pick here. [Source](https://www.g2.com/compare/clay-com-clay-vs-hunter)

| **Estimated total at least $7,587 (list-price floor) | |** | | |

Math: $2,975 + $495 + $999 + $2,500 + $49 + $495 + $49 + $25 = $7,587.00/mo (list-price floor). Assumptions: 40+ GTM people across teams, 25 of them prospecting in Apollo (Organization, billed annually, 3-seat minimum), ~25 LinkedIn senders (HeyReach Agency tier), monthly list prices except Apollo and Common Room (billed annually, Common Room 5 seats). Clay is its Growth monthly list price; its Enterprise tier is custom. Salesloft (outbound) has no public price and counts as $0 here; expect a per-seat, annual quote with a seat minimum. Peec AI is Advanced's monthly list price; SSO needs its Enterprise quote. Enterprise tiers, SSO and security documents are quote-based. This total is a floor, not a quote. Estimate only; excludes taxes, add-ons, overages and annual discounts. Prices as of 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-23 (per tool), verify with vendor. "from" and "quote" rows are not final prices.

## CRM for this team size (separate from the stack)

For 40+ GTM people: **[Salesforce Sales Cloud](https://www.salesforce.com/sales/)**, Core (replaces Enterprise Edition), 40 seats × $195 billed annually; expect a quote, about **from $7,800/mo**. Runner-up: **[HubSpot Sales Hub](https://www.hubspot.com/products/crm)**, Enterprise, 40 seats × $150, plus $3,500 one-time onboarding, about $6,000/mo + $3,500 one-time. Not included in the stack total above.

|  | CRM | Tier / assumption | Est. cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pick | **[Salesforce Sales Cloud](https://www.salesforce.com/sales/)** | Core (replaces Enterprise Edition), 40 seats × $195 billed annually; expect a quote | from $7,800/mo |
| Runner-up | **[HubSpot Sales Hub](https://www.hubspot.com/products/crm)** | Enterprise, 40 seats × $150, plus $3,500 one-time onboarding | $6,000/mo + $3,500 one-time |

Salesforce has the largest enterprise reviewer base among the CRMs we checked (33.7% of its G2 reviewers are enterprise). Plan for a longer rollout. If you send with Instantly, its native Salesforce integration retires on December 10, 2026 (OutboundSync or Zapier are the documented replacements).

### Spreadsheet or CRM?

At 40+ the CRM is the system of record; seat counts and admin rules matter more than the list price.

Signals that it is time for a CRM (our rules of thumb, not benchmarks):

- **A second person works the pipeline.** A cofounder, first seller, contractor SDR or agency. Shared sheets struggle with ownership, duplicates and overwritten notes.
- **More than about 20–30 live deals or conversations at once.** Or a follow-up has slipped more than once.
- **You copy sequencer replies into the sheet by hand.** More than about 30 minutes a week. Most CRMs here receive replies from Instantly, Smartlead or lemlist directly.
- **Email and LinkedIn reach the same people.** One record per person stops you double-touching prospects.
- **Investor or board pipeline reporting takes more than about an hour a month.** Stage history and pipeline reports are built into every CRM listed, including free plans (depth varies).
- **Inbound leads arrive or your first sales hire starts.** Forms, routing and activity history make the handoff work.

Starter sheet columns: Company, Contact, Email, LinkedIn URL, Source, Stage, Next step, Next-step date, Deal value, Last touch, Notes. Every CRM listed imports a CSV, so nothing is lost when you switch. List prices as of 2026-11-10 from vendor pricing pages; verify with the vendor. Seat counts follow this page's assumptions. [All CRMs we list](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/crm).

## What we found: who reviews these tools and enterprise readiness (as of 2026-11-05)

Security and plan statements come from each vendor's own pages and are vendor claims; reviewer company-size shares come from G2's public comparison pages . Overall G2 star ratings and review counts, when we have a dated check, appear on each tool card and feed the sentiment part of the value score. Company-size segment ratings are not in the file yet (G2 product pages were blocked). Everything may change; confirm security, SSO and compliance in writing before buying. This is not legal or compliance advice.

- **Apollo (list building).** Pricing page: Organization is $119 per seat per month billed annually with a 3-seat minimum, and SSO appears in its plan table (checked 2026-11-05). Trust center lists SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001, GDPR and CCPA. Help center has an article on setting up SSO. Vendor enterprise page cites RBAC, permission profiles and audit logging; vendor customer story: Superside runs 130 reps on Apollo. These are vendor statements. [Source](https://www.apollo.io/pricing)
- **Apollo (G2 reviewer size).** G2 comparison page (checked 2026-11-05): of 9,858 Apollo reviews, 67.0% small-business (50 or fewer employees), 28.4% mid-market (51-1,000) and 4.6% enterprise (over 1,000). That is roughly 2,800 mid-market and 450 enterprise reviewers (our arithmetic from G2's percentages). [Source](https://www.g2.com/compare/apollo-io-vs-clay-com-clay)
- **ZoomInfo (not in our stack: contact sales).** G2 reviewers (8,728 reviews, checked 2026-11-05) are 25.8% small-business, 48.1% mid-market and 26.1% enterprise, the most enterprise-heavy list-building voice we found. It publishes no price (priced by licenses and credits). Vendor security materials state SOC 2 Type II and ISO certifications. Request a quote next to Apollo's. [Source](https://www.g2.com/compare/clay-com-clay-vs-zoominfo-sales)
- **Clay (enrichment).** Vendor pricing page (checked 2026-11-05): states SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, GDPR and CCPA. Enterprise (custom pricing, annual commitment) adds SSO/SAML, SCIM, RBAC, user groups with credit budgets, IP allowlists, and a custom CSA and DPA; Launch and Growth do not include SSO or RBAC. Named customer case studies on the page include Intercom, Verkada, Rippling and Hex. Growth is $495/mo monthly list ($446 annual view). G2: 234 reviews, 73.8% small-business, 24.8% mid-market, 1.4% enterprise; Hunter (659 reviews) shows 31.9% mid-market. [Source](https://www.clay.com/pricing)
- **Salesloft (outbound, our Large pick).** G2 comparison page (checked 2026-11-05): 4,287 reviews, 16.5% small-business, 50.9% mid-market, 32.6% enterprise; G2 ease of setup 8.6 vs Outreach 7.7, quality of support 8.6 vs 8.3. Vendor security page lists SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO 27001; its security measures document also lists ISO 27701; help center documents SAML SSO (Okta, OneLogin, Google, Microsoft Entra). Trust center is public. Pricing page goes to a talk-to-sales form (no list price). Vendor says Salesloft is now the company and platform brand after merging with Clari. [Source](https://www.g2.com/compare/outreach-vs-salesloft)
- **Salesloft (security and SSO).** Security & compliance page and help center (checked 2026-11-05). [Source](https://www.salesloft.com/security-compliance)
- **Outreach (outbound, also consider).** G2 comparison page (checked 2026-11-05): 3,574 reviews, 19.1% small-business, 59.2% mid-market, 21.7% enterprise; reviewers flag cost and a steeper learning curve more often. Vendor trust page lists SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, ISO 27701, ISO 42001 and HIPAA, but trust center access is through an account exec. Pricing page lists Amplify Essentials, Core, Plus and Pro with 10,000 to 100,000 AI credits and says pricing is per user plus consumption; no list price. [Source](https://www.outreach.io/pricing)
- **Reply.io and HeyReach spot-check.** Reply.io, our previous Large outbound pick, is 80.5% small-business, 17.4% mid-market, 2.1% enterprise (1,568 G2 reviews), so it moved to the all-tools list as a cheaper option. HeyReach (LinkedIn) has only 74 G2 reviews, so the LinkedIn pick is unchanged and no listed LinkedIn tool has a large enterprise review base. [Source](https://www.g2.com/compare/outreach-vs-salesloft)
- **Common Room.** Vendor security page lists a SOC 2 Type 2 report, GDPR and CCPA compliance, SSO/SAML/SCIM and role-based access control. [Source](https://www.commonroom.io/security/)
- **Reply.io.** Help center documents organization, multi-team and single-team roles and permissions; vendor white-label page says the platform is SOC 2 certified. [Source](https://support.reply.io/hc/reply-help-center/articles/roles-permissions-tab)
- **HeyReach.** Help center documents Admin and Member roles with per-feature permissions. Its data processing addendum says SSO (including SAML) is not currently supported, and we found no SOC 2 claim. [Source](https://help.heyreach.io/en/articles/11782284-how-to-invite-team-members-and-manage-role-based-permissions-in-heyreach)
- **Hunter.** Help center: unlimited team members at no extra cost on one shared credit pool, with Owner, Admin and Member roles. Vendor says a DPA is included and SOC 2 is for enterprise. [Source](https://help.hunter.io/en/articles/15654553-hunter-account-faqs)
- **Instantly.** Public sources we found disagree on whether a SOC 2 Type II report is held. Ask the vendor for its current report under NDA before buying. [Source](https://instantly.ai/dpa)
- **Peec AI (AEO pick) and Profound.** Peec pricing page (checked 2026-11-05): Starter $95, Pro $245, Advanced $495 per month; SOC 2 on every plan; SSO only on Enterprise (custom). Profound pricing page: Enterprise custom with SOC 2 and SSO/SAML; self-serve brand plans are not published. Vendor claims; we did not collect G2 reviewer-size data for AEO tools. [Source](https://peec.ai/pricing)

## Scoring

### How does Profitable Agent Stack score tools?

When a dated G2 rating is on file: value\_score (0-100) = round(0.5 x fit + 0.3 x cost\_score + 0.2 x sentiment\_score). fit = editorial fit\_score (1-5) x 20. cost\_score = 100 - 60 x (entry\_price - lowest entry price in the use case) / (highest - lowest); contact-sales tools get no cost or value score. sentiment\_score = round(clip((Bayesian average - 3.0) / 2.0 x 100, 0, 100)), where Bayesian average = (50 x 4.3 + review\_count x G2 rating) / (50 + review\_count). Tools without review data are labeled "no review data yet" and keep value\_score = round(0.625 x fit + 0.375 x cost\_score). The category-wide value score uses the overall G2 rating. When segment ratings exist later, stack pages prefer the rating for that team size (solo/small -> small business, early/scaling -> mid-market, large -> enterprise). Stack picks also weigh fit for the GTM team size (reviewer company-size mix, case studies, enterprise-readiness evidence). Full method: https://profitableagentstack.com/methodology

# Smartlead vs Instantly vs lemlist: which outbound tool fits a small GTM team?

by [Limor Sinay](https://profitableagentstack.com/advisory), Profitable Agent Stack | [Artificial Intelligence (AI)](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/category/ai), [Blog Posts](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/category/blog-posts)

Smartlead, Instantly and lemlist are outbound email sequencers, not full autonomous AI SDRs. For a 2–5 person GTM team, Instantly starts at $47/mo on Growth (email-only, 5,000 emails); Smartlead’s Base plan starts at $39/mo and is built around many mailboxes; lemlist’s Email plan starts at $69/mo monthly ($55 annual) and adds LinkedIn and other channels on Multichannel ($109/mo, or $87 annual). Salesforge (from $48/mo) and Woodpecker are other published-price options in the same use case. List prices last verified 2026-11-23; always verify with the vendor. Not advice.

**Direct answer:** If you already have a list and want a polished email-only sender, look at [Instantly](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/outbound-email#instantly) first (Growth $47/mo for 5,000 emails). If you need to run many mailboxes and care most about sending infrastructure, look at [Smartlead](https://profitableagentstack.com/go/smartlead) (affiliate; Base from $39/mo). If you want email plus LinkedIn and other channels in one sequence, look at [lemlist](https://profitableagentstack.com/go/lemlist) (affiliate; Email $69/mo monthly or $55 annual; Multichannel $109/mo or $87 annual). [Salesforge](https://profitableagentstack.com/go/salesforge) (affiliate; Pro $48/mo monthly) and [Woodpecker](https://profitableagentstack.com/go/woodpecker) (affiliate; price not yet captured in our file) sit in the same [outbound email / sequencing](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/outbound-email) use case when they fit. None of these, on its own, is the same job as an [AI SDR](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/ai-sdr).

Prices below are vendor list prices last verified 2026-11-23. Affiliate links (Smartlead, lemlist, Salesforge, Woodpecker) are marked; a commission never changes scores, prices or order. See our [disclosure](https://profitableagentstack.com/disclosure). Instantly has no affiliate link on this site.

## What job these tools actually do

All three send and sequence outbound email. They are often compared in the same search as “best AI SDR,” but that label is broader: an AI SDR product is supposed to research, write, send and hand off or book, which we cover separately under [AI SDR / agentic SDR](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/ai-sdr). If you are choosing a sequencer for a 2–5 person team, stay on this page. If you want the story of companies that *did* deploy AI SDRs, see [how real companies use AI for GTM](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/how-companies-use-ai-for-gtm).

## Side by side (published entry prices)

| Tool | Starting published price | What it is best used for on a small team | In our directory |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Smartlead](https://profitableagentstack.com/go/smartlead) (affiliate) | Base from $39/mo (the pricing page also lists Pro, Smart and Prime tiers) | High-volume email sending and many connected mailboxes | [Write-up](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/outbound-email#smartlead) |
| [Instantly](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/outbound-email#instantly) | Outreach Growth $47/mo (5,000 emails); Hypergrowth $107/mo (125,000 emails, 25,000 contacts) | Email-only outbound when you already have a list and want a straightforward sender | [Write-up](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/outbound-email#instantly) |
| [lemlist](https://profitableagentstack.com/go/lemlist) (affiliate) | Email $69/mo monthly ($55 annual), 50,000 emails/mo; Multichannel $109/mo ($87 annual) | Teams that want email plus LinkedIn and other channels in one sequence | [Write-up](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/outbound-email#lemlist) |
| [Salesforge](https://profitableagentstack.com/go/salesforge) (affiliate) | Pro $48/mo billed monthly ($29.20/mo billed annually); Growth $96/mo monthly ($58.40/mo annually). Annual prices as shown on 2026-11-23 may include a seasonal offer | Another published-price email sequencer when the plan shape fits | [Write-up](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/outbound-email#salesforge) |
| [Woodpecker](https://profitableagentstack.com/go/woodpecker) (affiliate) | Price not captured automatically — see the vendor page | A further sequencer option; we have not yet verified a public price in our file | [Write-up](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/outbound-email#woodpecker) |

[Reply.io](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/outbound-email#reply-io) is also in the directory (email volume tiers “starts from” $59 monthly). [Outreach](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/outbound-email#outreach) and [Salesloft](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/outbound-email#salesloft) are listed for larger teams and are contact-sales.

## How to choose, without a fake winner

**Choose Instantly** when the job is email-only outbound, you already have (or can buy) a list, and you want the lowest published Growth-tier entry among the well-known three ($47/mo for 5,000 emails). It is the recommended outbound pick on our [small GTM team](https://profitableagentstack.com/stages/small-gtm-team) stack.

**Choose Smartlead** when mailbox count and sending infrastructure are the constraint — agencies and teams that connect many inboxes. A [Smartlead customer story about Pump.co](https://www.smartlead.ai/case-study/case-study-claire-hardesty) (vendor-published, updated 3 March 2026) describes nearly 800 accounts and about 130,000 emails in month one, with “close to $200K in pipeline revenue” attributed to those campaigns. That volume is not a default small-team setup; it is evidence the product is used at high send volume. Read the source, and see the [AI for GTM roundup](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/how-companies-use-ai-for-gtm) for the caveats.

**Choose lemlist** when you want one sequence that can include LinkedIn and other channels, not only email. The Multichannel plan is the one that adds those channels, at a higher published price. If you prefer a dedicated LinkedIn tool beside a cheaper email sequencer, [HeyReach](https://profitableagentstack.com/go/heyreach) (affiliate) and [Waalaxy](https://profitableagentstack.com/go/waalaxy) (affiliate) are in [LinkedIn outreach](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/linkedin).

**Add Salesforge or Woodpecker later, when they fit** — for example if a plan, workflow or existing vendor relationship matches your team better than the three above. We do not treat a missing price (Woodpecker) as a reason to dismiss the tool; we mark it unverified and point you to the vendor.

## What this does not decide

- **Deliverability** depends on your domains, warmup, copy and list quality, not only on the logo you pick. We do not publish a deliverability ranking of these three.
- **Enrichment is a different job.** [Clay](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/enrichment#clay), [FullEnrich](https://profitableagentstack.com/go/fullenrich) (affiliate) and [Hunter](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/enrichment#hunter) live on the [enrichment](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/enrichment) page.
- **An AI SDR is a different job.** Tools such as [Artisan](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/ai-sdr#artisan) and [Qualified](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/ai-sdr#qualified) are contact-sales in our file. SaaStr’s first-party posts on using them are summarized in [how real companies use AI for GTM](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/how-companies-use-ai-for-gtm). For most 2–5 person teams, that is an “add later” category.

List prices last verified 2026-11-23. Always verify with the vendor. General information only, not advice.

[Articles](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/) › How real companies use AI for GTM (sourced results)

# How real companies use AI for GTM (sourced results)

by [Limor Sinay](https://profitableagentstack.com/advisory), Profitable Agent Stack | [Artificial Intelligence (AI)](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/category/ai), [AI for GTM](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/category/ai-for-gtm), [Blog Posts](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/category/blog-posts)

Named companies have published what happened after they put AI into go-to-market, and the pattern is consistent: AI scales a motion that already works, and it takes daily human training. SaaStr’s first-party posts say agents first-touch-sourced $4.8 million in added pipeline and $2.4 million in closed-won revenue after eight months, with 15–20 hours of management a week from each of two leaders. Vendor-published stories from monday.com, Payhawk, Pump.co and Asana report time savings and pipeline or booking gains, each cited to the original page below. This is not advice; verify with the sources, and treat vendor case studies as the vendor’s account.

**Direct answer:** The useful “AI for GTM” evidence is not a generic leaderboard. It is a small set of named companies describing a specific motion, the tools they used, and a result, with a link you can open. First-party posts (the company writing about itself) are stronger than vendor case studies. Vendor case studies can still be useful if you read them as the vendor’s account and follow the original link. None of the numbers below were invented for this page.

## How to read this page

- **First-party** means the company published the numbers itself. **Vendor-published** means the tool vendor (or its blog) published the customer story. We label each one.
- Figures are copied from the linked source, with the wording the source used (for example “pipeline revenue” is not the same as closed revenue).
- Tools named below are linked to our [directory](https://profitableagentstack.com/directory) write-ups when we list them. Some affiliate links are marked in the relevant sections; a commission never changes scores or order. See our [disclosure](https://profitableagentstack.com/disclosure).
- A 2–5 person GTM team should not copy an enterprise build. Use the takeaway, then check our [small GTM team stack](https://profitableagentstack.com/stages/small-gtm-team).

## SaaStr: first-party, a small team running many agents

SaaStr is the closest public write-up we have of a tiny team running AI across go-to-market and publishing the numbers.

In *6 Months of AI SDRs: What’s Worked, How They Brought In $1M+ in 90 Days, and the Real Data Everyone’s Asking For* ([SaaStr, Jason Lemkin](https://www.saastr.com/6-months-of-ai-sdrs-whats-worked-how-they-brought-in-1m-in-90-days-and-the-real-data-everyones-asking-for/)), Lemkin and Chief AI Officer Amelia Lerutte wrote that they were running five specialized agents and that:

- Outbound agents (they say “primarily [Artisan](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/ai-sdr#artisan)”) sent 19,847 messages in six months, with a 6.7% overall response rate and a 4% positive response rate.
- They compare that with 3,000 emails per month from AI versus 75–285 per month from previous human reps.
- An inbound agent ([Qualified](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/ai-sdr#qualified)), added later, was credited with $1M+ in closed revenue in 90 days, $2.5M+ in pipeline from agent-booked meetings, 100+ meetings, and 70% of October’s closed-won deals.
- 20% of event ticket revenue “now comes from AI agents selling directly.”
- They say each of them spends 15–20 hours a week managing the agents, and they budget $50–100K per specialized platform per year.

A later first-party update, *What We Actually Learned Deploying 20+ AI Agents Across Our Entire Go-To-Market (8 Months In)* ([SaaStr, Jason Lemkin](https://www.saastr.com/what-we-actually-learned-deploying-20-ai-agents-across-our-entire-go-to-market-8-months-in/)), raises the aperture to 20+ agents “with just 3 humans and a dog” and reports:

- $4.8 million in additional pipeline first-touch sourced from an agent
- $2.4 million in closed-won revenue first-touch sourced from an agent
- deal volume more than doubled, win rates nearly doubled
- more than 60,000 AI-generated emails on the sales side
- the same 15–20 hours a week of maintenance, from each of Lemkin and Lerutte
- the results were “additive” and did not, in their telling, cannibalize existing inbound

That later post also describes stitching [Clay](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/enrichment#clay), Artisan, Qualified and Salesforce Agentforce together, and says marketing-orchestration tools were less mature than sales agents, which is why they built some of their own marketing agents.

**What a small team can take from this:** SaaStr’s own advice is to put an agent on work that is already proven, or on work the team is simply not doing (ghosted leads, small follow-ups), and to plan for daily training. They say an AI SDR will not fix outbound that does not already work with humans. Contact-sales AI SDR tools belong in the “add later, when the motion already books meetings” bucket for most 2–5 person teams; see [AI SDR / agentic SDR](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/ai-sdr) and [when to skip intent data](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/when-to-skip-intent-data).

## monday.com + Exa: vendor-published, list building for agents

Source: [monday.com x Exa case study](https://exa.ai/customers/monday), retrieved 24 November 2026 (America/New\_York). This is Exa’s customer story.

monday.com (Tel Aviv and global) describes building lead agents on [Exa](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/list-building#exa) Search so a rep can describe a segment in natural language and get structured companies and contacts from the live web. The page reports:

- 2.7 million enrichments completed “across the monday.com customer base”
- 50% less research time per SDR/AE, per prospecting cycle
- a “top 10 leads for the day” list waiting in monday CRM when a rep opens it

Daniel Lereya, Chief Product and Technology Officer, is quoted saying agents need “live intelligence” and that “Exa is where that comes from.” The same page is clear that a general-purpose LLM, on its own, did not produce usable emails, phone numbers and firmographics.

**What a small team can take from this:** “Ask an LLM to build my list” is not the same as a list-building or [enrichment](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/enrichment) tool with structured, sourced outputs. If you already have a list and need verified emails or mobiles, [FullEnrich](https://profitableagentstack.com/go/fullenrich) (affiliate) is the waterfall enrichment option we have an affiliate link for; [Hunter](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/enrichment#hunter) and [Clay](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/enrichment#clay) are the other published-price options in that use case. Compare them on the [enrichment](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/enrichment) page.

## Payhawk + Clay: vendor-published, better account selection

Source: [How Payhawk rebuilt outbound with Clay and grew pipeline 3x](https://www.clay.com/customers/payhawk), retrieved 24 November 2026 (America/New\_York). This is Clay’s customer story. Payhawk is a London-headquartered spend management company.

Clay’s story, quoting CRO Gabriela Belnikolovska and VP of Revenue Operations Richard Standring, says Payhawk grew pipeline 3x by rebuilding an outbound motion that was already one of its strongest channels. The page says they:

- gave each BDR 100 high-fit named accounts
- expanded account scoring from three or four inputs to roughly 25 parameters
- added signals such as new CFO appointments and former Payhawk users joining a new company
- saw median deal size for outbound-sourced customers rise 70%
- saw 50% more reps hitting or exceeding quota each month
- saw partner-sourced leads reach win rates of up to 60% in some months

The through-line is not “we bought an AI SDR.” It is account selection and timing, with research written back into Salesforce and the sequencer so reps see *why* an account is on the list.

**What a small team can take from this:** Clay’s Launch plan is $167/mo on the annual-billing view ($185 monthly) in our file, last verified 2026-11-23 — a real cost for a 2–5 person team. Our [small GTM team stack](https://profitableagentstack.com/stages/small-gtm-team) still treats a full Clay build as something to add when a simpler [enrichment](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/enrichment) and [outbound](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/outbound-email) motion already books meetings. When you do want Clay, it is in the directory; [FullEnrich](https://profitableagentstack.com/go/fullenrich) (affiliate) remains the dedicated waterfall option.

## Pump.co + Smartlead (and HeyReach): vendor-published, high-volume outbound

Source: [Pump.co Sent >130K Emails and Generated $200K in Revenue with Smartlead](https://www.smartlead.ai/case-study/case-study-claire-hardesty), published 24 February 2026, updated 3 March 2026. This is Smartlead’s customer story, written by a Smartlead staff writer.

Pump.co is described as a Y Combinator-backed cloud cost optimization startup. The case study says founding GTM engineer Claire Hardesty built outbound from scratch with [Smartlead](https://profitableagentstack.com/go/smartlead) (affiliate) and that in the first month they:

- sent approximately 130,000 emails (ahead of a 100,000-a-month goal)
- generated “close to $200K in pipeline revenue attributed directly to Smartlead campaigns”

Note the body wording: **pipeline revenue**, not necessarily closed-won revenue. The headline on the same page says “$200K in Revenue.” We quote the body.

The story also says they housed nearly 800 email accounts in Smartlead, used [Clay](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/enrichment#clay) to route sends into local business hours across seven campaign types, and supplemented LinkedIn outreach with [HeyReach](https://profitableagentstack.com/go/heyreach) (affiliate). Copy was written in-house with Smartlead’s spintax features.

**What a small team can take from this:** 130,000 emails in a month and 800 mailboxes is a volume motion, not a default 2–5 person setup. The transferable idea is a clear sequencer plus enrichment plus, when it fits, a LinkedIn tool. For published-price sequencers see [Smartlead vs Instantly vs lemlist](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/smartlead-vs-instantly-vs-lemlist) and [outbound email / sequencing](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/outbound-email). [HeyReach](https://profitableagentstack.com/go/heyreach) (affiliate) and [Waalaxy](https://profitableagentstack.com/go/waalaxy) (affiliate) are the LinkedIn tools we have affiliate links for; [Expandi](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/linkedin#expandi) is also in the directory.

## Asana + Workato: vendor-published, an internal GTM engine

Source: [How Asana Built an AI Engine for GTM with Workato](https://www.workato.com/the-connector/asana-gtm-ai-engine/), Perri Bronson, 30 September 2026. This is Workato’s account of a talk by Maschal Malek, Product Manager for Enterprise AI at Asana.

Asana started with more than 100 possible use cases, then shipped four: competitive intelligence, pre-call planning, post-call planning, and account summaries. Reps had been spending about 10 hours a week researching across eight or more tools. The team of six, each spending 15 hours a week on top of their jobs, stitched together tools Asana already owned (including Salesforce, 6sense, ZoomInfo, Chorus, Databricks, OpenAI and Workato) rather than buying a new AI suite. Malek is quoted saying a generated account or prospect brief cost about 10 cents per record.

In the first quarter after a sales-kickoff launch to 260+ reps, the page reports:

- a 10% increase in bookings (annual recurring revenue closed)
- account research time cut from 10 hours a week to 1
- 2.3× higher email reply rates than previous outreach
- 86% adoption in that first quarter, later 100% after adjustments for some enterprise account structures

They later added a custom MCP server and a Claude plugin so reps could ask account questions without writing back to Salesforce.

**What a small team can take from this:** the win came from orchestrating data the team already had, starting with a narrow set of jobs, and keeping a human in the loop for drafts and feedback. You do not need Asana’s 260-rep rollout to borrow that sequence. ZoomInfo is in our directory as a contact-sales [list-building](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/list-building#zoominfo) option for larger teams; it is not what we recommend first for a 2–5 person stack.

## A pattern you can use on a 2–5 person team

Across these write-ups, the companies that publish results do a few un-glamorous things first:

1. **They start with a motion that already works**, or with work nobody is doing. SaaStr says this explicitly.
2. **They keep a human trainer in the loop.** Two SaaStr leaders, and Asana’s six-person build team, all report serious weekly hours.
3. **They separate list building, enrichment, sending and (sometimes) AI SDR.** Pump.co used Smartlead + Clay + HeyReach. monday.com used Exa for live list and enrichment data inside its own CRM agents. Payhawk used Clay to decide *who* and *when*, not as a sender.
4. **They measure a specific outcome** (research hours, reply rate, pipeline, closed-won, bookings) and they say whether the figure is first-touch, influenced, pipeline or closed.

If you are choosing tools rather than reading stories, start here:

- [Stacks by GTM team size](https://profitableagentstack.com/stages/) and the [small GTM team](https://profitableagentstack.com/stages/small-gtm-team) stack
- [Outbound email / sequencing](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/outbound-email) and [Smartlead vs Instantly vs lemlist](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/smartlead-vs-instantly-vs-lemlist)
- [Enrichment & verification](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/enrichment)
- [LinkedIn outreach](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/linkedin)
- [AI SDR / agentic SDR](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/ai-sdr) — add later, when it fits
- [AEO (AI search visibility)](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/aeo), including [Otterly.AI](https://profitableagentstack.com/go/otterly-ai) (affiliate), if you care about being cited in AI answers

Prices in our directory were last verified 2026-11-23. Always verify with the vendor. General information only, not advice.

[Articles](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/) › When to add AEO (AI search visibility) vs classic SEO

# When to add AEO (AI search visibility) vs classic SEO

by [Limor Sinay](https://profitableagentstack.com/advisory), Profitable Agent Stack | [Artificial Intelligence (AI)](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/category/ai), [Blog Posts](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/category/blog-posts)

AEO tools track whether ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google's AI answers mention your brand. Classic search tools come first; add AEO when AI assistants already send you visits.

AEO (answer engine optimization, also called GEO) tools run a set of buyer questions through AI assistants and report whether your brand is mentioned or cited. Classic SEO tools tell you how you rank in search results. They are different jobs, so we list them as separate use cases: **Search performance**, **Content optimization** and **AEO (AI search visibility)**.

## A simple order

1. **Search performance first.** Google Search Console is free and shows which queries bring visitors. Most AI answers still draw on pages that rank, so this data helps both.
2. **Content optimization when you publish weekly.** A tool like Surfer helps each page match what searchers want. Before you publish regularly, it is a bill.
3. **AEO when AI search is a channel.** Add a tracker once AI assistants already send you visits you can see in your analytics, or your buyers say they ask ChatGPT first.

## What it costs

On the [published prices](https://profitableagentstack.com/directory) we checked: Peec AI starts at $95/mo for 50 prompts on 3 models, Otterly.AI at $29/mo for 15 prompts, and AthenaHQ and Scrunch at $295 and $250/mo. Profound is contact sales. Compare that with the $41/mo for a whole solo stack.

## What we recommend by size

- **Solo founder and small team:** skip. Warm leads and outbound produce more pipeline, and you have too little AI-search traffic to measure.
- **Early scaling and up:** one dedicated tracker. See the [early scaling stack](https://profitableagentstack.com/stages/early-scaling).
- **Large teams:** check SSO and security terms; several vendors reserve SSO for an enterprise quote.

## A caution

These tools measure answers that change from run to run, and none can guarantee a mention. Treat the numbers as a trend, not a score.

General information only, not advice. Prices as of 2026-11-23; verify with the vendor.

Published Nov 11, 2026


[Articles](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/) › Why we size stacks by GTM team size, not funding stage

# Why we size stacks by GTM team size, not funding stage

by [Limor Sinay](https://profitableagentstack.com/advisory), Profitable Agent Stack | [Artificial Intelligence (AI)](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/category/ai), [Blog Posts](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/category/blog-posts)

Funding rounds say little about what tools you need. How many people do go-to-market says a lot.

Two companies can raise the same round and have very different go-to-market teams: one founder selling alone, the other with fifteen people. They need different tools and should pay different amounts.

## The five sizes

- **Solo founder:** 1 GTM person
- **Small GTM team:** 2–5
- **Early scaling:** 6–15
- **Scaling:** 16–40
- **Large / multi-team:** 40+

## What changes as the team grows

- **Cost shifts from tools to seats.** Per-sender and per-seat pricing starts to dominate around the point where several people run LinkedIn outreach.
- **Admin matters.** At some size you need roles, permissions and a way to offboard people.
- **Signals earn their place later than you think.** See [when to skip intent data](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/when-to-skip-intent-data).
- **Procurement shows up.** Large teams need security documents and sometimes a sales call, and we say so when a tool is contact-sales.

## How we pick tools for each size

A tool's value score is category-wide and leans on its lowest published price, so a free plan can make a tool look like the best value for every team. For each size we also check who reviews and uses the tool: G2's reviewer company-size shares (50 or fewer employees, 51-1,000, over 1,000), customer stories that name team size, and for large teams security and admin evidence such as SSO, roles and SOC 2. That is why the 40+ stack counts a paid Apollo plan and picks Clay for enrichment, while solo and small stacks stay cost-first. Details are on the [methodology page](https://profitableagentstack.com/methodology).

## Where to start

Pick your size on the [stacks hub](https://profitableagentstack.com/stages/). Each page lists who it is for, the recommended stack with an estimated monthly cost, the use cases that matter at that size, the ones to skip, and the best-value tool for each job we include.

Sizes are planning bands, not rules. Estimates are not advice; verify prices with vendors.

Published Nov 9, 2026


[Articles](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/) › When to skip intent data (and what to do first)

# When to skip intent data (and what to do first)

by [Limor Sinay](https://profitableagentstack.com/advisory), Profitable Agent Stack | [Artificial Intelligence (AI)](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/category/ai), [Blog Posts](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/category/blog-posts)

Intent and signals tools help you prioritize. If you have nobody worth prioritizing yet, they are an expensive distraction.

Intent and signals tools answer one question: *who should I contact first?* That is a great question once you have a list, a message and a sequence that sometimes gets replies. Before that, it is a bill.

## A simple test

Skip paid intent data until **all three** are true:

1. Your hand-built outbound already books meetings. Not once, repeatedly.
2. You have more good-fit accounts than you can contact this month.
3. A better order of contact would change what you do on Monday.

If any of these is false, spend the time on your message and your list instead.

## What it costs to be early

On the [published prices](https://profitableagentstack.com/directory) we checked: RB2B has a free plan and a Starter plan at $79/mo, while Common Room's Essential plan is $2,500/mo billed annually for 5 seats. A solo founder's whole recommended stack costs about $41/mo. Paying for intent data first can cost more than the rest of the stack combined.

## What to use instead

- **Solo founder:** skip signals entirely. Message your warm network and send simple outbound. See the [solo founder stack](https://profitableagentstack.com/stages/solo-founder).
- **Small GTM team:** the free RB2B plan is enough, and only once meetings are already coming in.
- **Early scaling:** a low-cost visitor-identification tool starts to earn its place.
- **Scaling and above:** signals belong in the core stack. Pay for them when a real prioritization problem exists.

## One more caution

Visitor identification and intent data raise privacy and consent questions that depend on where your buyers live. Check your obligations before you switch anything on.

General information only, not legal or financial advice. Prices as of 2026-11-23; verify with the vendor.

Published Nov 6, 2026


[Articles](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/) › One tool per job: how to stop paying twice

# One tool per job: how to stop paying twice

by [Limor Sinay](https://profitableagentstack.com/advisory), Profitable Agent Stack | [Artificial Intelligence (AI)](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/category/ai), [Blog Posts](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/category/blog-posts)

Most GTM stacks pay for the same job two or three times. Here is how we pick one tool per job and explain each pick.

Tool sprawl is quiet. A sequencer here, a second enrichment plan there, and a scheduler nobody opened since March. Each is small; together they are a real line on the budget.

## The rule

For every use case, pick **one** tool, write down why, and revisit it monthly. Our recommended stacks follow that rule with no paid overlap, and each row on a stack page says why that tool won.

## How to choose

1. **Name the job narrowly.** "Outbound email sequencing" is a job. "Sales automation" is not.
2. **Start from the free tier.** Several jobs are covered at $0 (for example Google Search Console for search data, or a free newsletter plan). Prove you need more before paying.
3. **Compare on value, not features.** We rank tools in each use case by [value score](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/how-we-score), then explain any pick that is not the top score.
4. **Count seats honestly.** Per-sender or per-seat pricing, such as LinkedIn tools, is where costs grow fastest as the team grows.

## When two tools in one stack is fine

Two tools are fine when they do **different** jobs. In our stacks, Search Console tracks search performance while Surfer optimizes content, and RB2B identifies site visitors while PostHog analyzes product usage. That is two jobs, not one job paid for twice.

## See it in practice

The [stacks by GTM team size](https://profitableagentstack.com/stages/) show one pick per job at each size, with the monthly estimate and the use cases we would skip.

General information only. Prices change; verify with vendors. Prices as of 2026-11-23.

Published Nov 4, 2026


[Articles](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/) › How we score AI GTM tools (and why cost counts)

# How we score AI GTM tools (and why cost counts)

by [Limor Sinay](https://profitableagentstack.com/advisory), Profitable Agent Stack | [Artificial Intelligence (AI)](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/category/ai), [Blog Posts](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/category/blog-posts)

The value score in plain words: what goes in, what does not, and why money never changes rank.

Every tool in the [directory](https://profitableagentstack.com/directory) gets one number: a **value score** from 0 to 100. Here is exactly what is behind it, so you can disagree with it intelligently. (Updated 23 November 2026, when verified G2 ratings were added to the score.)

## What goes in

- **Fit (50%).** An editorial 1–5 judgment of how well the tool does its one job, converted to 0–100. It is an opinion, and we say so.
- **Cost (30%).** Inside each use case, the lowest published starting price scores 100 and the highest scores 40, scaled in between. A tool with no public price gets no cost score and therefore no value score.
- **Sentiment (20%).** A public G2 rating with a source link and the date we checked it, converted to 0–100 with a confidence shrink for low review counts. Tools we have not yet checked are labeled "no review data yet," and fit and cost carry the score (62.5% and 37.5%).

## How sentiment is calculated

1. Bayesian average: (50 × 4.3 + review count × rating) / (50 + review count). The 4.3 prior is a typical G2 B2B rating; 50 reviews is the weight of that prior. A tool with few reviews is pulled toward 4.3; a tool with thousands of reviews stays close to its raw rating.
2. Map 3.0 → 0 and 5.0 → 100, and clip to that range: sentiment = clip((Bayesian average − 3.0) / 2.0 × 100, 0, 100), then round to an integer.

Example: Instantly's G2 rating is 4.8 from 4,167 reviews (checked 23 November 2026). Bayesian average = (50 × 4.3 + 4,167 × 4.8) / (50 + 4,167) = 20,216.6 / 4,217 = 4.794. Sentiment = (4.794 − 3.0) / 2.0 × 100 = 90 (rounded). Fit is 5/5 → 100 and the cost score is 84, so value = 0.5×100 + 0.3×84 + 0.2×90 = 93.

Capterra figures, when we have them, stay in the notes for context and are not used in the score. We never invent ratings.

The category-wide value score uses the overall G2 rating. When reviewer-segment ratings exist later (small business: 50 or fewer employees, mid-market: 51–1,000, enterprise: over 1,000), a stack at a given team size will prefer the matching segment rating (solo and small → small business, early and scaling → mid-market, large → enterprise). If a segment rating is missing, we fall back to the overall rating. Segment ratings are not in the current data.

## What stays out

- **Affiliate links and sponsorships.** Payment never changes a score, a badge or an order. See the [affiliate disclosure](https://profitableagentstack.com/disclosure).
- **Prices we could not verify.** Those are shown as "price not yet verified" instead of guessed.

## Where the cost estimates come from

Each stack on the [stacks-by-GTM-size hub](https://profitableagentstack.com/stages/) adds up published monthly list prices for the stated tiers and seats, with the math shown. They are estimates: they exclude taxes, add-ons, overages and annual discounts, and prices change. Always verify with the vendor.

## Scores do not pick the stack alone

The score ranks tools within one use case. For a stack at a given team size we also weigh who reviews the tool at that size and, for large teams, enterprise readiness such as SSO and security documents. When the two disagree, for example a free plan that tops the score but is not what a 40-person team would run, we follow the size evidence and explain why on the stack page.

## The honest limits

A score cannot know your market, your data or your team. Use it to shortlist, then run a trial. The full method lives on the [methodology page](https://profitableagentstack.com/methodology), and if you spot an error, the [corrections page](https://profitableagentstack.com/corrections) is the fastest way to tell us.

General information only, not professional, legal or financial advice. Prices as of 2026-11-23.

Published Nov 2, 2026


## Page: https://profitableagentstack.com/methodology

# How do you rank tools and choose stacks?

Value score (0–100) = 50% use-case fit + 30% cost + 20% user sentiment, when a verified G2 rating with a source link and date is on file. Tools without review data keep a 62.5% / 37.5% fit/cost reweight and are labeled "no review data yet." Contact-sales tools still get no cost score and no value score. Recommended stacks do not use the score alone: each pick also has to fit the GTM team size, based on reviews from companies of that size and enterprise-readiness evidence.

## How we choose a stack pick for a team size

Two checks, in this order. (a) Value score: it ranks tools inside one use case and is driven by the lowest published starting price, which is often a free plan, so it favors tools that are cheap to start. (b) Fit for that GTM team size: we look for who actually reviews and uses the tool, using G2 reviewer company-size shares (small business: 50 or fewer employees, mid-market: 51–1,000, enterprise: over 1,000), vendor case studies that name team size, and for large teams security and admin evidence (SSO, roles, SOC 2, data processing terms). If a high-scoring tool is mostly reviewed by small teams, or its free plan is not what a 40-person team would run, the stack uses a paid tier with a quote flag, or a different tool, and says why. Solo and small stacks stay cost-first because free and entry plans still match those sizes.

## What size-segmented evidence we show

On the Scaling and Large stack pages we list what we found, with the source link and the date checked. We show reviewer company-size shares from G2's public comparison pages and link to the filtered review pages. Overall G2 star ratings and review counts now appear on tool cards when we have a dated check (taken from G2 search-result cards, because product pages were blocked). Company-size segment ratings are not in the file yet; when they are, stack pages will prefer the segment that matches the team size (see Sentiment score). Counts such as "roughly 2,800 mid-market reviewers" are our arithmetic from G2's percentages and are labeled that way. Reviewer mix is a signal, not proof: it shows who talks about a tool, not how well it works for your team.

## Limits

Some job categories have no listed tool with a large mid-market or enterprise review base (outbound and LinkedIn outreach, for example). We say so on the Large page rather than pretend otherwise. Contact-sales tools such as ZoomInfo get no value score because they have no public price, and may appear as an option to quote rather than in the priced stack.

## Fit score (editorial)

An editorial 1–5 judgment of how well the tool serves its use case, converted to 0–100 (×20). It is an opinion, not a measurement, and is reviewed when vendors or readers send corrections.

## Cost score

Within each use case, the lowest published starting price scores 100 and the highest scores 40, scaled linearly. Tools without a public price (contact sales or not yet verified) get no cost score and no value score.

## Sentiment score

When we have a verified public G2 rating (source link and date checked), we convert it to a 0–100 sentiment score with a confidence shrink for low review counts, then give it 20% of the value score.

1. Bayesian average: (50 × 4.3 + review count × rating) / (50 + review count). The 4.3 prior is a typical G2 B2B rating; 50 reviews is the weight of that prior. A tool with few reviews is pulled toward 4.3; a tool with thousands of reviews stays close to its raw rating.

2. Map 3.0 → 0 and 5.0 → 100, and clip to that range: sentiment = clip((Bayesian average − 3.0) / 2.0 × 100, 0, 100), then round to an integer.

Example: Instantly's G2 rating is 4.8 from 4,167 reviews (checked 2026-11-23). Bayesian average = (50 × 4.3 + 4,167 × 4.8) / (50 + 4,167) = 20,216.6 / 4,217 = 4.794. Sentiment = (4.794 − 3.0) / 2.0 × 100 = 90 (rounded). Fit is 5/5 → 100 and the cost score is 84, so value = 0.5×100 + 0.3×84 + 0.2×90 = 93.

Capterra figures, when we have them, stay in the notes for context and are not used in the score. We never invent ratings.

When reviewer-segment ratings exist (small business: 50 or fewer employees, mid-market: 51–1,000, enterprise: over 1,000), the category-wide value score still uses the overall rating. For a stack at a given team size we prefer the matching segment rating (solo and small → small business, early and scaling → mid-market, large → enterprise), using that segment's share of reviews as the count when a share is published. If a segment rating is missing, we fall back to the overall rating. Segment ratings are not in the current data (G2 product pages were blocked; TrustRadius install figures are not used as review segments), so every score today uses the overall rating.

Tools without review data are labeled "no review data yet" and keep the 62.5% fit / 37.5% cost reweight. Contact-sales tools can still show a rating, but they get no cost score and therefore no value score.

## CRM is shown separately

Each team-size page has its own CRM section with a pick, a runner-up and when a spreadsheet is enough. CRM costs are not added to stack totals, because many teams already have a CRM or start on a spreadsheet.

## Stack cost estimates

Sum of published monthly list prices for the stated tiers, seats and volumes on each GTM-team-size page. Labeled estimates; excludes taxes, add-ons and overages.

## Money never changes rank

Sponsorships and affiliate links do not change scores, prices or order.

## Page: https://profitableagentstack.com/review-policy

# How do you handle reviews and ratings?

We never fabricate, buy or edit reviews or ratings. We show only public ratings from G2 or Capterra with a source link and date checked, or a link to the reviews.

## Third-party ratings

Ratings belong to their sources and are shown as of the date checked. They may change. G2 and Capterra are trademarks of their owners and do not endorse us.

## Reader feedback

Feedback submitted through "Share your experience" (not live yet) may be moderated. We will not publish it as a rating, and we will remove content that is fake, abusive, defamatory or from someone with an undisclosed conflict of interest. Vendors may not review their own products.

## Incentives

We do not offer incentives for reviews. If that changes, incentivized feedback will be labeled.
